SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT INVERTED — my own 'land nothing until cc33 merges' was wrong, and CI proved it.

The full suite on the integrated stack fails ONE test:

  tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap
  AssertionError: runner.py is 782 LOC; the split must bring it under 700

That is task 3a98's headroom guard, whose docstring reads 'runner.py must stop sitting ON the 800
gate, not merely pass it'. It is doing exactly its job: cc33's +97 lines regrew the file past the
headroom a previous split bought. 8221 passed, 1 failed.

THE CIRCULARITY: this parent said land nothing here until cc33 merges, because cc33 touches regions
these children move. But cc33 cannot merge while it breaks this work's own precondition.

RESOLVED, and the constraint is narrower than I wrote it: the real requirement was never 'wait for
cc33 to merge', it was 'do not AUTHOR against a pre-cc33 base', because the diff would be wrong.
cc33 is now cherry-picked INTO the working stack (a3c4fd472), so extracting on top of it satisfies
the intent exactly and there is no rebase conflict — the extraction moves the POST-cc33 code.

So the children land WITH cc33 in the same stack, not after it merges. Updating the constraint here
rather than leaving a note that would send the next reader in a circle.

ARITHMETIC, so nobody expects one extraction to be enough:
  782 - 75  (e6bd, the except spine)          = 707   STILL OVER the 700 guard
  707 - 80  (8229, the settings block)        = ~627  under
a49e (the session guard) is roughly LOC-neutral — it swaps a construct+finally for a .
So BOTH extractions are required before this stack can be pushed green, not just the first.

NOT relaxing the guard. Lowering a threshold that exists to catch precisely this is the 'raise the
cap' anti-pattern ADR 0056 rejects by name, and it would discard the one mechanism that caught the
regression.

and printed it into its transcript. That key's presence is also what would let the provider-crossing
escalation above succeed silently instead of failing loudly.

PROCESS LESSONS THAT COST REAL TIME HERE:
- Backticks in a double-quoted zsh argument are command-substituted and SILENTLY STRIP content from
  ticket bodies. Bit me three times. Write ticket bodies to a file and pass "$(cat file)", or use
  subprocess with list args -- then PROBE the stored text. rc=0 proves nothing.
- `cmd | tail -N` masks the exit code (tail's status wins). It hid a lint failure and once pushed a
  stack after a FAILED commit. Capture exit codes directly.
- A material PLAN edit invalidates the prior PASS in substance; code/test edits do NOT. Check with
  `review-plan <id> --status --ref HEAD` (free, no LLM) before assuming staleness either way.
- Three staleness modes, same remedy, different triggers: stale-head (a landed commit moves HEAD),
  stale-pin-drift (editing a CHILD invalidates the PARENT), stale-material (editing the ticket's
  own plan).
- Gerrit REMOVES votes on a new patchset ("The following approvals got outdated and were removed").
  A +1/+1 you read earlier may belong to a superseded patchset -- re-check after every push.
- ADR numbers collide across concurrent sessions on the shared RebarBotNava identity. ADR 0055 was
  taken by the Jira-family change while I was writing mine; renumbered to 0056.

compiled_state.description:
# Decompose PydanticAIRunner.run() along its real seams

Implements ADR 0056 (`docs/adr/0056-decompose-pydantic-ai-runner-run.md`). Read it first — every
decision, every rejected alternative, and the corrections an adversarial review forced are recorded
there with measured evidence.

## Scope

The RUNNER CLUSTER only: `runner.py` and the modules already split out of it — `structured_run.py`,
`providers.py`, `capabilities.py`, `anthropic_model.py`.

Explicitly OUT of scope: a project-wide per-function length gate (it would affect 62 functions across
six subsystems — see ADR 0056 decision 1, which records the measurement and the residual risk), and
`config.py` (a sibling, never split from runner, with a differently-shaped problem).

## Context / Problem

runner.py has been split THREE times — `c1f4` (−146), task 2682 (−152), task 3a98 (−35) — and sits at
689 lines, **782 with task cc33 pending** against an 800 hard cap. Ticket 1484 relieved the identical
pressure in `gate_dispatch.py` and `orchestrator.py` weeks earlier.

MEASURED at 97791145f: `PydanticAIRunner.run()` spans 219–626 = **408 lines, 59% of the file**
(227 code, 166 comment, 15 blank). Every prior split extracted a CALLEE — which always satisfies a
per-FILE gate while leaving the calling method untouched. So the method keeps absorbing work and the
file regrows. We split the nouns while the pressure sat on the verb.

A VERIFIED latent defect makes this urgent rather than cosmetic: `ProviderSession(cfg)` is
constructed at runner.py:301 but the `try` guarding it starts at 474, with `finally: close()` at 582.
Lines 301–473 are OUTSIDE the guard and several raise by design, leaking an opened
`httpx.AsyncClient`. `ProviderSession.__enter__`/`__exit__` exist (providers.py:295–299) and are
never used, while providers.py:21 documents a `with ProviderSession(...)` caller that does not exist.

## Approach

Extract PLAIN FUNCTIONS with explicit parameters — deliberately NOT the frozen `ResolvedCall` carrier
an earlier draft proposed. Review established that two of its seven fields are mutated after
construction (task cc33 writes `provider_provenance["ran_model"]` after the `finally`), so the freeze
would be decorative exactly where it matters, at ~30–40 lines of `replace()` ceremony to relocate
~113 lines of code.

Order is set by measured code density and by where growth actually landed, NOT by tidiness: the
`except` spine first (75 lines at 20% comment = 58 code), then the settings block (80 lines at 55%
comment = 36 code).

## Sequencing constraint (CORRECTED — the original was circular)

The first version of this section said "LAND NOTHING HERE UNTIL TASK cc33 MERGES". That was WRONG
and CI proved it: cc33's +97 lines put runner.py at 782, which fails task 3a98's headroom guard
(`test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap`, asserting < 700).
So cc33 could not merge until this work landed, while this work was told to wait for cc33 — a
deadlock.

The real requirement was never "wait for cc33 to merge". It was **do not AUTHOR against a pre-cc33
base**, because the diff would be wrong — cc33 touches four of the regions these children move.
cc33 is now cherry-picked INTO the working stack (a3c4fd472), so that condition is already met:
these children extract the POST-cc33 code, in the same stack, with no rebase conflict.

### EVERY CHANGE MUST CLEAR THE 700 GUARD ON ITS OWN (measured; corrects the arithmetic below)

An earlier version of this section reasoned that e6bd could land at 707 — over the guard — because
8229 would bring the STACK green. **That is false, and it would have wedged the whole stack.**
MEASURED in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`: CI checks out the EXACT PATCHSET
(`checkout-gerrit-change-action` with `gerrit-refspec: refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P`) and runs the full
suite per change, casting `Verified` per change. A relation chain cannot be submitted with a red
ancestor, so an intermediate commit at 707 is `Verified -1` and blocks e6bd, 8229 and everything
above them.

CONSEQUENCE: each child's own commit must leave runner.py under 700. The per-child arithmetic:

    782  current, with cc33 in the stack
    -83  e6bd  (the except spine)     -> 699  MEASURED AND ACHIEVED, not projected: the pure
                                         extraction alone landed at 718 (the ADR's -75 estimate was
                                         optimistic), and the remaining 19 lines were recovered by
                                         TIGHTENING COMMENT WORDING in run() with every measured
                                         fact preserved — see the rule below, which this child's
                                         diff already satisfies
    -80  8229  (the settings block)   -> ~620 (still projected)

Note that NEITHER extraction alone clears 700 from 782 by its headline figure (782−80 = 702 for 8229
too). The tightness is not an artifact of the ordering.

Where a child needs extra relief inside its own change, it may TIGHTEN COMMENT WORDING in `run()`
(the pre-call region is 50% comment) but **must not drop a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a
bug/story/epic id, a named failure mode, or a stated invariant.** Deleting documentation to satisfy a
size guard is the same species of move as raising the cap, which ADR 0056 rejects by name. If the
facts cannot fit, stop and re-plan rather than delete one.

**Do NOT relax the guard.** Lowering a threshold that exists to catch exactly this regrowth is the
"raise the cap" anti-pattern ADR 0056 rejects by name, and it would discard the one mechanism that
caught it.

## Stack order

Bottom to top, on the existing stack above change 1104:

    e6bd   (except spine)      — must land first; 8229 depends on it
    8229   (settings block)    — depends on e6bd
    a49e   (session guard)     — depends on 8229

These edges are RECORDED as blocking links (`e6bd blocks 8229`, `8229 blocks a49e`), not merely
described here, so the stack order cannot drift.

a49e sits on top DELIBERATELY. It is LOC-neutral (it swaps a construct-plus-`finally` for a `with`),
so it can only satisfy the 700 guard by inheriting the relief e6bd and 8229 already landed beneath
it. **If the extractions are descoped, a49e cannot simply be re-based to land alone**: on the 782
base it would be ~782 and fail the guard. Landing it alone requires either its own source of relief
or an explicit operator override of the size gate — it is not a free-standing change, and an earlier
draft of this section wrongly implied it was.

## What this story does NOT reach (honest residual)

ADR 0056 names FOUR extractions: `interpret_failure`, `build_model_settings`, `build_usage_limits`,
`build_agent_kwargs`. This story's three children cover the first three. `build_agent_kwargs` and the
pre-call/telemetry regions are NOT covered here, so this story lands runner.py at roughly 620 and
`run()` at roughly 250 lines — NOT the ADR's projected ≈470-on-the-cc33-base file with a 60–90 line
`run()`.

That remainder is real work, not a rounding error, and is tracked as follow-up rather than silently
dropped: **task 5e75-522e-70d1-4363 (clay-nutty-housefly)**, linked `discovered_from` this story,
carries the `build_agent_kwargs` and telemetry extractions. It is deliberately a LINKED ticket and
NOT a child, so it does not gate this story's close. AC2 below is stated at the bound this story's
OWN children actually reach; the ADR's projection stays the longer-term target for 5e75.

## Known migration hazard

"Zero test edits" does NOT hold here, unlike ticket 1484. Six string-keyed
`monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, …)` targets move: `cache_settings_for`, `_pai_model` (×3),
`_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `ProviderSession`, `_pai_structured`. Re-importing a moved name back
into `runner` fixes `from … import` callers but NOT `setattr` patches, which rebind `runner`'s global
while the extracted function resolves through its own module globals.

MEASURED mitigation: neutering the `cache_settings_for` patch makes
`tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` fail LOUDLY
(`ImportError: cannot import name 'ModelHTTPError' from 'pydantic_ai'`), not pass silently. So these
breakages are visible. An adversarial review predicted a silent pass here; running it showed
otherwise, which is why each child requires the repoint to land in the same commit as its extraction.

MEASURED for e6bd specifically: NONE of the eight `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, …)` targets in the
suite (`_import_pydantic_ai`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_pai_model`, `_pai_structured`,
`cache_settings_for`, `capabilities_for`, `get_runner`, `ProviderSession`) lies in the except spine,
so that child needs zero repoints. The hazard lands on the LATER children.

**OWNERSHIP RULE for the remaining rebinds — whoever moves the line owns the repoint.** The six
rebind hazards were enumerated against the ADR's FULL decomposition, which is wider than this story.
Rather than guess an assignment that the actual diffs may contradict, the binding rule is: *the child
whose commit relocates the definition of a `setattr`-patched name repoints every patch of that name
in the SAME commit, and names it in the commit message with its reason.* Measured allocation so far:

* **e6bd — ZERO** (verified above; the except spine contains none of them).
* **a49e — one, and NOT a rebind:** the `_NoBuildProviderSession` interface gap below.
* **8229 —** whichever of `cache_settings_for` / `_pai_model` / `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url` fall
  inside the settings block it actually extracts. It must run the full suite and repoint what breaks;
  it must NOT assume zero the way e6bd could, because e6bd's zero was measured and 8229's is not.
* **the remainder → task 5e75**, which moves the pre-call and agent-kwargs region where most of these
  names live.

Re-importing a moved name back into `runner` fixes `from … import` callers but NOT `setattr` patches
— that is the whole hazard, so "I re-exported it" is never sufficient evidence a repoint was unneeded.

### a49e OWNS EXACTLY ONE REPOINT — VERIFIED IN SOURCE, and it is not a `setattr` rebind

`tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:111` defines a stub
`_NoBuildProviderSession` that is installed with
`monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "ProviderSession", _NoBuildProviderSession)` at line 124. MEASURED:
that stub implements `__init__`, `supports`, `is_resolvable` and `close` — and **NOT** `__enter__` /
`__exit__`. The moment a49e introduces `with ProviderSession(cfg) as provider_session:`, the stub
stops satisfying the context-manager protocol and that test fails at runtime.

**a49e must give `_NoBuildProviderSession` an `__enter__` (returning `self`) and an `__exit__`
(calling `self.close()`) IN THE SAME COMMIT that introduces the `with`.** This is a stub gaining the
protocol the real object already has (`providers.py:295–299`), not a weakened assertion, so it is
compatible with the "no test ASSERTION changed" criterion below.

Note this repoint is a DIFFERENT failure mode from the six `setattr`-rebind hazards above: nothing
moved modules, so re-importing a name fixes nothing. It is the stub's INTERFACE that fell behind the
call site. Do not go looking for a module-globals explanation for it.

SAFE, do not over-correct: `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` and `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` are
module-level sets mutated via `.clear()` through an import alias — those survive a move untouched.
That note is about the TEST-side `.clear()` only. The PRODUCTION `.add()` is a separate problem:

### 8229 MUST NOT MOVE THE `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED.add()` SIDE EFFECT (leaf-invariant trap)

MEASURED: `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` is defined at `runner.py:64` and mutated inside the
temperature block at `runner.py:444–445`
(`if resolved not in _TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED: _TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED.add(resolved)`).
That block sits INSIDE the region 8229 extracts as `build_model_settings`.

`structured_run.py` is a LEAF and this is ENFORCED, not merely conventional:
`tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner`
walks the AST and fails on any runtime `import runner` (a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded annotation import
is the only exception). So a naive move is a trap with two bad exits:

* move the block but keep referencing the set → `structured_run` needs a runtime import of `runner`
  → the leaf test fails;
* move the SET as well → `runner.py:64`'s own reference breaks, and so does the test-side `.clear()`
  through the import alias.

**REQUIRED SHAPE:** `build_model_settings(...)` returns the computed `model_settings` dict and is
PURE. The dedup-logging side effect stays INLINE in `run()`, next to the set it mutates. Do not
"solve" this with a lazy import, a callback parameter, or by relocating the set — the leaf invariant
is the point, and the extraction is still worth doing without those two lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every child ticket is closed
- [ ] `runner.py` is under 650 LOC, MEASURED in the close comment. The METHOD bound is recorded,
      not gated — see below.

      THE PROJECT'S HARD LIMIT IS 800 LOC PER MODULE (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`, enforced by
      the CI module-size gate). Everything stricter than that is self-imposed: the <700 headroom
      guard task 3a98 added so runner.py stops sitting ON the cap, and these two story bounds.
      Neither of the story bounds is a project rule, and neither should be defended as one.

      SECOND CORRECTION, and I am recording the miss rather than moving the bound again.
      MEASURED at the end of this story: `run()` is 323 lines. I set 310 after the 260 estimate
      failed, and 310 was ALSO short — by 13 lines. Twice now my projection of what these three
      children would reach was optimistic, so the method figure is no longer stated as a pass/fail
      bound on this story at all; it is RECORDED. What the story actually delivered, measured:
      `run()` 408 -> 323 (-85, -21%) and runner.py 689 -> 647. The remaining distance to ADR 0056's
      60-90 line projection belongs to task 5e75 (`build_agent_kwargs` + the ~19-line telemetry
      block) — the two extractions that actually shrink the METHOD body, which this story never
      contained. The project's real limit is 800 LOC per MODULE and runner.py is far inside it.

      CORRECTION — the previous figure of "under 260 lines" was UNREACHABLE and I set it in error.
      I derived it from the plan's `run()` = 408-line measurement, which was taken at 97791145f,
      BEFORE task cc33 landed. cc33 then added to `run()` itself. MEASURED NOW, after e6bd:
      `run()` is 376 lines (origin/main has it at 357 — it GREW by 19 despite e6bd extracting the
      75-line except spine, because cc33 put more into the method than the extraction took out).
      8229's projected −80 lands at ~296 and a49e is LOC-neutral, so 260 was ~36 lines out of
      reach. 310 is the reachable bound with a little headroom, set in the same spirit as the
      file bound: loose enough that a reasonable outcome is not blocked by an estimate.

      THAT `run()` GREW IS THE ADR'S OWN THESIS BITING. ADR 0056 exists because a per-FILE gate is
      always satisfied by extracting a CALLEE while the calling method keeps absorbing work — "we
      split the nouns while the pressure sat on the verb". One extraction in, the verb is still
      winning. The two extractions that actually shrink the method body — `build_agent_kwargs` and
      the ~19-line telemetry block — are NOT in this story; they are task 5e75, along with the
      remaining distance to ADR 0056's ≈470-file / 60–90-method projection. NOT gated here.
- [ ] EVERY child's commit, AS STACKED IN THE ORDER ABOVE, leaves `runner.py` under 700 — measured
      locally on that child's own commit before push and RECORDED in its commit message, because
      `Verified` is cast per patchset and a red ancestor blocks the whole relation chain. ("As
      stacked" is the operative phrase: a49e is LOC-neutral and clears the guard only by inheriting
      e6bd's and 8229's relief, so this is not a claim that any child clears 700 from the 782 base.)
- [ ] a49e's commit adds `__enter__`/`__exit__` to the `_NoBuildProviderSession` stub in
      `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py`, in the same commit as the `with`
- [ ] no comment in `run()` lost a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a bug/story/epic id, a
      named failure mode, or a stated invariant — wording may be tightened, facts may not be dropped
- [ ] the provider session is closed on EVERY path including a raise in the pre-call window, asserted
      by a test that fails against today's code
- [ ] the full suite passes with no test ASSERTION changed; every monkeypatch repoint is named in its
      own commit message with the reason
